widthOnlyClearingExamples.scope: Closed-form measurement of the captured via/trace pair on unchanged final centerlines; no DRC or routing rerun, no global validity inference.

identityMethod: Exact production TraceWidthSolver.getNominalTraceWidthForRoute resolution on captured srjWithPointPairs.connections; exact getPipeline9RouteIndexByTraceId for all final participant traces; actual converted circuitJson via id mapping plus addAutoroutingViaTraceIds/getPipeline9DrcErrorTraceIds. No parsed guessed connection IDs or proximity identity joins.
conclusions: No captured initialHD effective width is below the requested0.095mm minimum. The generic A03 ignoring a0.15/0.2 requested width defect is not observed under this case's actual0.095 request.

InitialHD routes are narrower than resolved per-connection nominal widths, and many captured joint/final routes contain wider copper. This is an existing staged width model difference, not proof that it caused this experiment's regression.

Closed-form width-only measurements can show which existing via/trace clearances on final centerlines depend on wider copper, but cannot infer which route geometry an earlier width-aware solver would produce or whether the complete board would be clean.
The10 final via-via drill errors are unaffected by reducing trace width. No attribution of all92 errors or the old-vs-new outcome difference to width is supported without additional evidence.
captureLinkageLimit: Initial-HD geometry came from the separate already-captured early-stop execution on the same source and fixture; point-pair newConnections are byte-identical to the full failing capture, but its full earlier route geometry was not preserved. Width semantics and exact connection identities agree; no claim that both runs' entire earlier geometry is identical.
